note: Papers are those where an Aurora member (faculty, coordinator, postdoc, or student) is the first or second author. Authorship was checked against the arXiv author list; publication status ('venue') was verified via CrossRef/journal_ref. Links point to the ADS record. 'person' is the member who is first/second author. Do not add papers where no member is first or second author, and do not add unverified papers, awards, figures, or venues.

items.title: First statistical study of over 100 magnified stellar events at z ≈ 0.72 with JWST
items.blurb: The first statistical sample of over 100 highly magnified individual stars at z ≈ 0.72, detected with JWST as microlensing transients near galaxy-cluster critical curves, opening a new probe of distant stellar populations and small-scale dark matter.

items.title: The kinematically hot, extremely metal-poor C-19 stellar stream in DESI DR2
items.blurb: Using DESI DR2 radial velocities and metallicities to characterize the C-19 stream, whose large velocity dispersion is hard to explain with a purely baryonic, disrupting globular-cluster progenitor.

items.title: A new free-form lens model of AS1063 from ultra-deep GLIMPSE imaging
items.blurb: A new free-form lens model of the cluster AS1063 built from spectroscopically confirmed lensed galaxies and ultra-deep GLIMPSE imaging, which confirms and uncovers new lensed systems including a yellow-supergiant candidate at z ≈ 3.

items.title: Black hole merger rates in the first billion years in light of JWST data
items.blurb: Modeling black-hole merger rates in the first billion years to test light- versus heavy-seed scenarios against the abundance of faint AGN that JWST finds at z = 4–9.

items.title: The ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST Survey: JWST/IFU optical observations of 18 main-sequence galaxies at z = 4–6
items.blurb: The ALPINE-CRISTAL-JWST survey combines kpc-resolved HST, JWST, and ALMA imaging and spectroscopy of 18 main-sequence galaxies at z = 4–6 to resolve their stars, gas, and dust together.

items.title: The superclustering of hot gas: cosmological sensitivity in the WebSky simulations
items.blurb: Orientation-aware summary statistics of the superclustering of hot gas in the WebSky simulations, sharpening the cosmological sensitivity of thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich and galaxy cross-correlations.

items.title: The WebSky [CII] forecasts and the search for primordial intermittent non-Gaussianity
items.blurb: WebSky [CII] line-intensity mock maps that forecast upcoming wide-field submillimeter surveys (matched to CCAT) of cosmological [CII] emission from the epoch of reionization.

items.title: Quantitative morphology of Galactic cirrus in deep optical imaging
items.blurb: A morphological study of optical Galactic cirrus in deep imaging, using intensity statistics, angular power spectra, and wavelets to characterize the diffuse interstellar medium.

items.title: Synergising semi-analytical models and hydrodynamical simulations to interpret JWST data from the first billion years
items.blurb: Feeding cold-gas fractions and star-formation efficiencies from the SPHINX20 radiation-hydrodynamics simulation into the DELPHI semi-analytic model to explain the abundance of bright galaxies at z ≥ 11 and the drivers of reionization.

items.title: GLIMPSE: an ultra-faint Pop III galaxy candidate and first constraints on the Pop III UV luminosity function at z ≈ 6–7
items.blurb: A NIRCam-based search across ~500 arcmin² of JWST legacy fields turns up GLIMPSE-16043, a promising ultra-faint Population III galaxy candidate at z ≈ 6.5, and sets first limits on the Pop III UV luminosity function.
